brief: Morgan Stanley frames four takeaways for the November 2026 US midterms. Prediction markets price 61% odds of a Democratic sweep of both chambers, 31% of Democrats taking the Senate only, and 7% of a Republican sweep. First, executive-led policy (tariffs, trade, deregulation, immigration, export controls) continues regardless of outcome; only fiscal policy (SNAP/Medicaid timing, defense spending, shutdown/debt-limit severity) is election-sensitive, and the deficit stays near 6% of GDP under every scenario with only about 0.2pp of variance either way. Second, the midterms are not a 2028 signal, since outcomes typically don't produce outsized 3-6 month market moves and midterm issues rarely carry into the next presidential race, but four debates (Social Security, individual taxes, data center restrictions, healthcare) via specific races and ballot measures could reveal where 2028 fault lines are forming. Third, AI sentiment splits: data center opposition is a real, mostly state-and-local catalyst where governor and utility-commission races matter more than Senate races, most constructive under a Republican sweep and least under a Democratic sweep, while AI safety regulation stays executive-led and unlikely to move absent a high-salience incident. Fourth, markets react mainly through sectors, Treasury supply and the dollar, not the macro outlook broadly.

cards.document: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
cards.claim: Prediction markets price the midterm outcome at 7% for a Republican sweep of the House and Senate, 61% for a Democratic sweep of both chambers, and 31% for Democrats winning the Senate while Republicans hold the House.
cards.anchor: 7% (R House, R Senate) 61% (D House, D Senate) 31% (D House, R Senate)

cards.document: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
cards.claim: Morgan Stanley currently expects the US deficit as a share of GDP to be around 6% over the next two years regardless of the midterm outcome.
cards.anchor: We currently expect the deficit as a share of GDP at around 6% in the next two years

cards.document: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
cards.claim: A Republican sweep could add about 0.2 percentage points of upside risk to the 2027 deficit as the OBBBA is implemented as written and defense spending runs above expectations.
cards.anchor: A Republican win could mean slight upside risk to the deficit in 2027, around 0.2pp

cards.document: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections

cards.anchor: A unified Democratic sweep could result in further deficit expansion of around 0.2pp as well through delays or rollbacks of scheduled SNAP and Medicaid cuts

cards.document: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
